acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Treants family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Elder Warden, T4, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Heartwood-Habitat Champion (Champion) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Ancient hollow trunk with amber heartwood cavity, nesting birds, and mushrooms along the base.

Signature mechanic: Hollow Council: birds leave one branch, non-luminous mushrooms unfurl at one root and catch reflected amber heartwood light rather than emitting light, and a vine screen grows between them before the cavity releases amber sap.
battlefieldDuty: Control alternating habitats by opening an amber heartwood cavity that directs birds, mushrooms, and vine screens.
constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T3 have no heartwood cavity, no waterfall, no boulders, and no groves; T4 alone gains the source-supported heartwood cavity; T5 alone carries its waterfall, boulders, and groves.
Compressed mineral root shoes, sediment bark laminates, crystal load knots, localized dust, and pale faults alter weight without treating native caught stones as affinity.
counterplay: Cross outside the marked pair and strike the open heartwood cavity after the sap release. Affinity signal: Tier-safe anchors: T1–T3 have no heartwood cavity, no waterfall, no boulders, and no groves, so a planted mineral root exposes a fracture; T4 heartwood cavity opens after a loaded stomp; T5 waterfall, boulders, and groves strain one crystal-bound root arch.
forbiddenTreatments: Treating ordinary stones in roots as Earth affinity
identityInvariants: Vertical trunk body, root-cluster legs, long branch arms, a bark-suggested face, and canopy remain recognizable.
Bark brown and grey, moss green, autumn gold, sap, and restrained amber heartwood remain botanical materials.
Nests, vines, mushrooms, bark runes, scars, and growth rings record age without replacing readable joints.
Girth, canopy, rooted reach, and resident ecosystems escalate while branch load and root commitment preserve counterplay.
telegraph: The hollow trunk opens, amber heartwood pulses, and mushrooms catch reflected amber heartwood light as residents move toward the selected branch-root pair; the mushrooms remain non-luminous.
